chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Boston band instrumentation and the union hangout
summary: Boston had good reeds, pianos and drummers but scarce brass; musicians hung out in a small union room to find gigs.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: What was the personnel or what was the size of the bands when you went gigging in Boston? You had saxophone. Was there a trumpet usually? Or did you have any brass?
They had brass. They had a trumpet when they could find one. Brass was not plentiful. Good trumpet players were not plentiful up there. Good brass was not plentiful.
So usually, if you got a dance to play...

I would try to get a trumpet, a couple of saxophones, and a rhythm section. Sometimes it would be one saxophone, a rhythm section, if you could a (?) trombone. But they were very scarce. Hard to get... No good brass up there. A lot of good reeds, a lot of good pianos and drummers, and things like that. But brass was not that good.
Now, you had a hangout for musicians, much like the Rhythm Club down here.

Mmm-hmm. That was at the Union. The Union had a little room, about half as big as this room. We used to go up there and hang around. You know, nothing much happening. We'd get jobs out of there and one thing or another. Or if you got a gig and want to meet some place, you could go up there and meet, sit around and play cards or something until it's time to go the gig.
